family: NULL-sensitive join condition simplification under NOT
setup: CREATE TABLE tl(a INT,b INT); CREATE TABLE tr(x INT,y INT);
left: SELECT tl.a,tl.b,tr.x,tr.y FROM tl JOIN tr ON NOT (tl.a = tr.x OR (tl.a IS NULL AND tr.x IS NULL))
right: SELECT tl.a,tl.b,tr.x,tr.y FROM tl JOIN tr ON NOT (tl.a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM tr.x)
note: Translated Spark's <=> null-safe equality to DuckDB's IS NOT DISTINCT FROM. DuckDB 1.5.1 itself applies the same unsound rewrite with its optimizer enabled, so both queries were executed after PRAGMA disable_optimizer to inspect SQL three-valued semantics.

family: EXCEPT to DISTINCT plus negated filter; alias rebinding
setup: CREATE TABLE repro_t(id INT,val INT);
left: (SELECT val AS id FROM repro_t) EXCEPT (SELECT val AS v FROM repro_t WHERE id=1)
right: SELECT DISTINCT val AS id FROM repro_t WHERE NOT coalesce(val=1,false)
note: DuckDB has no Spark USING parquet clause; plain in-memory table preserves the supplied rows and query semantics. The right query transcribes the issue's optimized logical plan.

family: IN subquery to existence join under NULL-observing predicate
setup: CREATE TABLE t(c INT); CREATE TABLE tn(c INT);
left: SELECT c FROM tn WHERE (c IN (SELECT c FROM t)) IS NULL
right: SELECT c FROM tn WHERE (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t WHERE t.c=tn.c)) IS NULL
note: In-memory tables replace Spark parquet tables with identical schema and contents. The right query models the non-nullable EXISTS attribute that replaces IN in the reported optimized plan.

family: DISTINCT aggregate expansion over empty input
setup: CREATE TABLE events(id INT,c1 VARCHAR,c2 VARCHAR);
left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT region),COUNT(DISTINCT channel) FROM (SELECT 'US' AS region,'web' AS channel,id FROM events)
right: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT region),COUNT(DISTINCT channel) FROM (SELECT 'US' AS region,'web' AS channel FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS seed FROM events) g)
note: Spark's VALUES-derived empty view is represented by an empty table with the same projected columns. The right query expresses the reported inserted global aggregate as a SQL subquery, which emits a row on empty input.

family: EXISTS subquery in LEFT JOIN ON converted to wrong nullable join condition
left: SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 id) t1 LEFT JOIN (SELECT 2 id) t2 ON t1.id=t2.id OR EXISTS(SELECT * FROM (SELECT 3 id) p WHERE p.id=t2.id)
right: SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1 id) t1 LEFT JOIN (SELECT 2 id) t2 ON t1.id=t2.id OR t2.id IS NOT NULL
note: SQL and inline values are from the Calcite issue. Right condition is derived from the exact faulty Rel condition printed in the issue: OR(=($0,$1), IS NOT NULL($1)); the EXISTS marker was replaced with the right input column. DuckDB rejects a non-inner join with a subquery, so the pair was run in SQLite 3.49.1. Historical Calcite 1.36.0 issue, fixed in 1.42.0.

family: ROWS window aggregate to grouped join
left: SELECT seq, sum(seq) OVER (PARTITION BY grp ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumsum FROM (VALUES (1,'A'),(2,'A'),(3,'A'),(1,'B'),(2,'B')) AS t(seq,grp) ORDER BY grp,seq
right: WITH t(seq,grp) AS (VALUES (1,'A'),(2,'A'),(3,'A'),(1,'B'),(2,'B')), totals AS (SELECT grp,sum(seq) AS cumsum FROM t GROUP BY grp) SELECT t.seq,totals.cumsum FROM t JOIN totals USING(grp) ORDER BY grp,seq
note: Right SQL spells out the GROUP BY plus INNER JOIN replacement described in the issue. PRAGMA disable_optimizer was set before both queries so DuckDB's source query was measured with SQL window semantics rather than any version-specific optimizer rewrite.

family: AVG reduction over all-NULL inputs
setup: CREATE TABLE dept(deptno INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,name VARCHAR(20)); CREATE TABLE emp(empno INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,deptno INTEGER REFERENCES dept(deptno),ename VARCHAR(20),job VARCHAR(20),mgr INTEGER,hiredate DATE,sal INTEGER,comm INTEGER,slacker BOOLEAN);
left: SELECT AVG(SAL), AVG(SAL) FROM EMP
right: SELECT AVG(SAL), CAST(CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE COALESCE(SUM(SAL), 0) END / COUNT(*) AS INTEGER) FROM EMP
note: Used the exact EMP rows from the issue fixture. Only the AVG column is retained from its wider rule-test projection. The Calcite rewrite is preserved; DuckDB integer division/cast semantics are exercised on the NULL-only input.

family: correlated COUNT subquery decorrelation to grouped inner join
setup: CREATE TABLE t1(a INT,b INT); CREATE TABLE t2(a INT);
left: SELECT a FROM t1 WHERE b IN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t2 WHERE t1.a=t2.a)
right: SELECT t1.a FROM t1 JOIN (SELECT a,COUNT(*) AS n FROM t2 GROUP BY a) q ON t1.a=q.a AND t1.b=q.n
note: Right SQL explicitly expresses the reported decorrelation into a grouped subquery and inner join; the empty correlated COUNT group is absent from that grouping. The issue's data values are preserved exactly.

family: correlated aggregate decorrelation drops empty-input row
setup: CREATE TABLE dept(deptno INT); CREATE TABLE emp(deptno INT,sal INT);
left: SELECT deptno FROM dept d WHERE 0 IN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM emp e WHERE d.deptno=e.deptno)
right: SELECT d.deptno FROM dept d JOIN (SELECT deptno,COUNT(*) AS n FROM emp GROUP BY deptno) q ON q.deptno=d.deptno AND q.n=0
note: The issue's report includes the equivalent condition and expected department 40; its sparse-data condition is preserved. Right query spells the described grouped-inner-join decorrelation, which loses the zero count for a no-match group.

family: empty-side anti-join pruning
setup: CREATE TABLE emp(id INT,dept_id INT); CREATE TABLE empty_dept(id INT);
left: SELECT e.id FROM emp e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM empty_dept d WHERE d.id=e.dept_id)
right: SELECT id FROM emp WHERE FALSE
note: The right query models the issue's incorrect reduction of an ANTI join over an empty right side to an empty result; the source gives a relational-plan example, not SQL/data, so this is an explicitly derived compact fixture.

family: OFFSET duplicated by SortJoinTransposeRule
setup: CREATE TABLE dept(deptno INT); CREATE TABLE emp(empno INT,deptno INT);
left: SELECT d.deptno,e.empno FROM dept d RIGHT JOIN emp e ON d.deptno=e.deptno ORDER BY e.empno OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY
right: SELECT d.deptno,e.empno FROM dept d RIGHT JOIN (SELECT empno,deptno FROM emp ORDER BY empno OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY) e ON d.deptno=e.deptno ORDER BY e.empno OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY
note: The Jira gives the exact relational plan but not executable SQL or table data. This is a minimal ordered RIGHT JOIN fixture encoding the reported plan's duplicated offset; SQL and rows are explicitly derived for a reproducible semantic counterexample.

family: partial-index constrained scan drops residual filter
setup: CREATE TABLE a(k INT PRIMARY KEY,a INT,b INT);
left: SELECT k FROM a WHERE a > 1 AND b > 3
right: SELECT k FROM a WHERE b > 3
note: The source uses Cockroach partial indexes on a and b; DuckDB does not support the same partial-index syntax. The source row and predicates are exact. The right query explicitly expresses the Cockroach plan's missing `a > 1` conjunct.

family: fractional DECIMAL equality range truncation on indexed integer
setup: CREATE TABLE t(c INT NOT NULL);
left: SELECT c FROM t WHERE c = CAST(0.06669620421124867 AS DECIMAL(20,18))
right: SELECT c FROM t WHERE c = CAST(0 AS INT)
note: The MySQL report uses `KEY(c)` and compares this predicate with `IGNORE INDEX(c)`. DuckDB does not implement MySQL index hints, so the left query is the row-by-row predicate and the right query explicitly expresses the truncated point range described in the issue. The source insert rows and decimal literal are exact.

family: GROUP BY lost when implicit min/max/count projection is used
setup: CREATE TABLE t(c0 UINT8);
left: SELECT c0,count(*) FROM t WHERE c0<>0 GROUP BY c0 ORDER BY c0
right: SELECT min(c0),count(*) FROM t WHERE c0<>0
note: The source uses a ClickHouse MergeTree partitioned by c0 and boolean `WHERE c0`; DuckDB has neither that storage engine nor implicit projection. The source rows are exact; `c0<>0` is the portable equivalent of ClickHouse UInt8's truthy `WHERE c0`. The right query makes the documented min/count projection shortcut explicit, which discards the group key.

family: CHECK-derived values cross-joined into semi-join input
setup: CREATE TABLE aa(a INT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE bc(b INT NOT NULL,c INT NOT NULL,CHECK(b IN (1,2,3)));
left: SELECT aa.a FROM aa WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bc WHERE aa.a=bc.c)
right: SELECT aa.a FROM aa CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1),(2),(3)) AS inferred(b) WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bc WHERE aa.a=bc.c)
note: Source includes a CHECK constraint and lookup index. Index syntax is omitted because DuckDB has different access-path planning; the three check-enumerated values and row data are retained. The right query is an explicit SQL form of the reported inferred-value cross product.

family: CHECK-derived branch expansion duplicates outer-join null extension
setup: CREATE TABLE t(x INT NOT NULL CHECK(x IN (1,3)),y INT NOT NULL,z INT,PRIMARY KEY(x,y));
left: SELECT u.y,t.x,t.y,t.z FROM (VALUES (1),(2000)) AS u(y) LEFT JOIN t ON u.y=t.y ORDER BY u.y,t.x
right: SELECT u.y,t.x,t.y,t.z FROM (VALUES (1),(2000)) AS u(y) LEFT JOIN t ON u.y=t.y AND t.x=1 UNION ALL SELECT u.y,t.x,t.y,t.z FROM (VALUES (1),(2000)) AS u(y) LEFT JOIN t ON u.y=t.y AND t.x=3 ORDER BY 1,2
note: The issue generates 1,000 y values for x=1 and x=3, then joins probe values 1 and 2000. Reduced the source data to the two rows needed for one match and the unmatched-key witness. Right query spells out the two CHECK-derived lookup branches whose UNION ALL duplicates the missing-side row.

family: NULL placeholder equality incorrectly converted to exact index span
setup: CREATE TABLE t(k INT PRIMARY KEY,a INT,b INT,UNIQUE(a));
left: SELECT k FROM t WHERE a = NULL
right: SELECT k FROM t WHERE a IS NULL
note: The Cockroach report uses a prepared parameter bound to NULL and tests generic-plan/index-span behavior. DuckDB cannot reproduce Cockroach plan caching; the left SQL expresses the row-by-row NULL equality semantics, while the right query expresses the reported mistaken exact-NULL lookup. Source data is preserved.

family: INT8 versus FLOAT comparison normalization rounds away a matching integer
setup: CREATE TABLE big(i BIGINT);
left: SELECT i FROM big WHERE i = 9007199254740992.0::DOUBLE
right: SELECT i FROM big WHERE i = CAST(9007199254740992.0 AS BIGINT)
note: The issue reports the left query as wrong in CockroachDB and identifies UnifyComparison constant type-unification as the cause. DuckDB evaluates the original comparison correctly. The right query is derived from the reported lossy rewrite: converting the FLOAT constant to the INT8 column type. Schema, value, and literal are from the issue.

family: sorted aggregate implementation drops empty-input scalar aggregate row
setup: CREATE TABLE emps(deptno INT);
left: SELECT max(deptno) AS m FROM emps WHERE deptno>100
right: SELECT max(deptno) AS m FROM emps WHERE deptno>100 HAVING count(*)>0
note: The issue supplies the same SQL under EnumerableAggregate and forced EnumerableSortedAggregate, with expected NULL row versus actual no rows. The right query is a portable SQL model of the sorted implementation’s empty-result behavior; the source does not give a second SQL text because only the planner implementation changes. The table is the minimal empty input satisfying the issue filter.

family: correlated NOT IN decorrelation replaces outer semantics with inner join
setup: CREATE TABLE emp(empno INT,job VARCHAR,sal INT); CREATE TABLE dept(deptno INT,name VARCHAR);
left: SELECT sal FROM emp e WHERE empno NOT IN (SELECT deptno FROM dept d WHERE e.job=d.name)
right: SELECT e.sal FROM emp e JOIN dept d ON e.job=d.name AND e.empno=d.deptno
note: The left query follows the issue’s correlated NOT IN SQL; aliases were added for clarity. The issue’s exact bad Rel plan changes the correlate/left semantics to an inner join with matching job and empno/deptno keys; the right SQL spells out that plan. The fixture is a minimal constructed counterexample because the issue does not provide table rows: one emp row and an empty dept table make NOT IN over an empty set true while the bad inner join drops it.

family: false-condition LEFT JOIN incorrectly propagated as empty relation
setup: CREATE TABLE table_3(int_col_6 INT); CREATE TABLE table_4(int_col_1 INT);
left: SELECT int_col FROM (SELECT coalesce(t2.int_col_1,t1.int_col_6) AS int_col FROM table_3 t1 LEFT JOIN table_4 t2 ON FALSE) t WHERE int_col IS NOT NULL
right: SELECT int_col FROM (SELECT coalesce(t2.int_col_1,t1.int_col_6) AS int_col FROM table_3 t1 LEFT JOIN table_4 t2 ON FALSE) t WHERE FALSE
note: The original Scala repro is translated to SQL with its exact values and LEFT JOIN ON false semantics. Spark reports the optimized result as LocalRelation <empty>; the right query is an explicit SQL form of that reported empty plan. The issue does not print a rewritten SQL statement, so this pair models the plan result rather than running Spark’s optimizer in DuckDB.

family: DELIM_JOIN statistics infer scalar subquery IS NULL as constant false
setup: CREATE TABLE test(x INT,y INT);
left: SELECT (SELECT y FROM test t2 WHERE t1.x=5) IS NULL FROM test t1
right: SELECT FALSE FROM test t1
note: The issue supplies the schema, rows, original query, and EXPLAIN projection showing the erroneous constant FALSE over a SINGLE DELIM_JOIN. Right SQL expresses that reported projection. DuckDB 1.5.1 no longer reproduces the historical optimizer bug on the source query; executing the direct before/after expressions yields TRUE twice versus FALSE twice and validates the semantic witness, not the current optimizer behavior.

family: correlated filter hoisted above unordered DISTINCT ON
setup: CREATE TABLE hoist_outer(k INT PRIMARY KEY,s INT); CREATE TABLE hoist_inner(k INT PRIMARY KEY,i INT,s INT);
left: SELECT o.k FROM hoist_outer AS o WHERE EXISTS(SELECT * FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (i) i,s FROM hoist_inner AS inner_t WHERE inner_t.s=o.s))
right: SELECT o.k FROM hoist_outer AS o WHERE EXISTS(SELECT * FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (i) i,s FROM hoist_inner AS inner_t) q WHERE q.s=o.s)
note: Schema, rows, and original correlated EXISTS query are from the issue. The right query expresses the exact reported hoist, moving s=o.s above DISTINCT ON. DISTINCT ON has arbitrary-row semantics without ORDER BY; in DuckDB 1.5.1 this input order selects s=10 before the filter, matching the issue’s documented empty result. Issue is on CockroachDB master and had not shipped in a release.

family: outer generator loses null-extension when projection pruning clears join flag
left: SELECT nil FROM (SELECT 1 AS x) x LEFT JOIN UNNEST([]::INTEGER[]) AS n(nil) ON TRUE
right: SELECT nil FROM (SELECT 1 AS x) x CROSS JOIN UNNEST([]::INTEGER[]) AS n(nil)
note: The source gives exact Spark SQL using LATERAL VIEW OUTER EXPLODE(array()), the join=false diagnosis, and a second query with x added. DuckDB expresses the outer generator as LEFT JOIN UNNEST and the faulty non-outer path as CROSS JOIN UNNEST; the fixture remains one input row and an empty generated relation. Issue affects Spark 1.5.2 and was fixed in 2.0.0.
